We have carbon NMR shifts: 161.40, 143.85, 130.30, 26.65, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20 ppm.

We need count of carbonyl groups. Carbonyl carbons appear around 160-220 ppm (for ketones, aldehydes, esters, acids). Here we have a peak at 161.40 ppm, maybe carbonyl (could be aromatic C attached to carbonyl? but typical carbonyl ~190-210 for ketone, 170-180 for ester, 200 for aldehyde). 161.40 could be conjugated carbonyl (like amide? Actually amide carbonyl ~165-175). So likely one carbonyl.

Other peaks: 143.85 aromatic, 130.30 aromatic, others aliphatic.

Thus count = 1.

We could verify with IR for C=O stretch ~1700 cm-1. Use ir_spectra.
